govdocs-archive_org-man-and-technics-osw: Oswald Spengler’s Man and Technics: A Contribution to a Philosophy of Life — from the Berserker archive — is his late essay on technology. The Decline of the West author’s pages are dark and prophetic. The book is a classic of cultural pessimism.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-FBIFeltWMark_FB: This CBS News item — Face the Nation: W. Mark Felt, August 29, 1976 — is a broadcast file. Felt was the FBI’s number two. He later emerged as Deep Throat. The interview is a time capsule. The file belongs to the press archive.
the-prince-of-graustark: Return to the imaginary Balkan kingdom of Graustark, the setting of George Barr McCutcheon's beloved romantic adventures. Prince Robin, heir to the throne, must win his crown while winning the heart of an American heiress. Sword duels, court intrigue, and palace balls fill the pages — a cheerful, old-fashioned tale of love and royalty in a storybook land.
beverly-of-graustark: George Barr McCutcheon returns to his imaginary kingdom of Graustark, where the American girl Beverly Calhoun finds herself entangled in royal romance and intrigue. Palace balls, daring escapes, and a prince in disguise fill this cheerful Ruritanian adventure. Pure romantic escapism from the master of the genre.
my-life-and-work: Henry Ford tells his own story — the farm boy who put America on wheels. His plain, forceful account of the Model T, the assembly line, and his ideas on work made this a bestseller. The autobiography of an age. His ideas on wages, work, and service changed industry forever, for better and worse.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-the-: A 1913 piece on the Abbey of the Park, by Louvain. Norbert's canons kept it for eight centuries. Francis Martin Geudens tells its tale. Brabant's quiet holy place. Rubens painted altarpieces for its church. Its fish ponds fed the canons in Lent.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ancient-see-o: A 1913 entry on the ancient see of Aarhus — Denmark's Jutland bishopric. Arthur Taylor tells its Catholic past. Its cathedral is the nation's longest. The Reformation ended the old line. A vanished see of the north. Its church is now a Lutheran cathedral.

A 1913 entry on the ancient see of Roskilde — the Danish primatial see. Arthur Taylor tells its royal story. Kings sleep in its brick cathedral. Absalon ruled as its bishop. Denmark's Westminster by the fjord. Its kings sleep in the brick chapels.

A 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia entry on the ancient see of Viborg — the Jutland bishopric. Arthur Taylor tells its medieval story. Its bishops served the northern parishes. The Reformation closed the old line. A vanished see of Denmark. Its cathedral keeps the old crypt.

This 1913 reference article on the ancient see of York — the northern primacy. Edwin Burton tells its proud story. Its minster crowns the old Roman city. Canterbury and York disputed the lead. England's second throne. Its chapter claims the northern primacy.
